decisions.decision: How should documents enter the system?
decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive daily, with volume varying strongly over the year. The design space offers batch and streaming ingestion approaches (d:7).

alternatives.label: Data ingestion in batches
pros: Seasonal peak scale: collect and process in batches
cons: Latency: results wait for a batch run

alternatives.label: Streamed data ingestion
cons: Seasonal peak scale: continuous capacity may be harder to right-size

decisions.rationale: Seasonal peak scale decides the choice: batches allow work to be grouped around fluctuating volume. This gives up immediate ingestion and classification.
consequences: Capacity must handle peak batch volume.

decisions.decision: Should classification processing be batched or real time?
decisions.context: The system classifies millions of documents daily, but the brief sets no response-time target. The design space frames batch and real-time processing as alternatives (d:15).

alternatives.label: Batch-based data processing
pros: Seasonal peak scale: process accumulated work in scheduled runs

alternatives.label: Real-time, stream-based data processing
cons: Seasonal peak scale: requires capacity for variable continuous load

decisions.rationale: Seasonal peak scale decides the choice because no latency target requires real-time processing. This gives up prompt per-document results.
consequences: Batch capacity must cover peak periods.

decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, and the brief specifies neither synchronous access nor a latency target. The design space includes scheduled batch output and real-time service options (d:5).

alternatives.label: Data batch based model serving
pros: Seasonal peak scale: write scheduled prediction batches to storage
cons: Team consumption: results are available only after runs

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
pros: Team consumption: teams can request real-time predictions
cons: Seasonal peak scale: service capacity must absorb demand peaks

decisions.rationale: Seasonal peak scale decides the choice given the lack of an immediate-response requirement. This gives up real-time access in favor of scheduled stored results.
consequences: Consumers need access to the results store.

decisions.decision: How should classification data and results be shared?
decisions.context: Multiple teams need classification results, and operators need evidence to assess quality drift. A shared store is one option in the design space (d:2).

alternatives.label: Shared data store
pros: Team consumption: common access point for results
cons: Team consumption: access boundaries need coordination

alternatives.label: Data service
pros: Team consumption: access can be mediated through services
cons: Seasonal peak scale: shared service capacity must handle demand

decisions.rationale: Team consumption decides the choice: a common store gives several teams access to batch results. This gives up service-mediated access controls and requires teams to coordinate access.
consequences: Teams depend on shared storage availability.

decisions.decision: How should production classification be monitored?
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. The design space distinguishes monitoring system data and predictions from monitoring model performance (d:22).

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Drift visibility: retain inputs and predictions for inspection
cons: Drift visibility: logs alone do not establish model quality

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
pros: Drift visibility: observe model performance parameters
cons: Drift visibility: requires suitable quality measures

decisions.rationale: Drift visibility decides the choice because the requirement is explicitly about classification quality. This gives up the broader operational trace that logging inputs and predictions can provide.
consequences: Monitoring requires a way to assess model performance.

decisions.decision: How should the model be adjusted when monitoring finds drift?
decisions.context: Drift visibility implies a response when quality degrades. The design space offers manual or automated model adjustment (d:24).

alternatives.label: Manual model adjustment
pros: Drift visibility: people review evidence before changing models
cons: Drift visibility: response may be delayed

alternatives.label: Automated model adjustment
pros: Drift visibility: automated action can follow detected changes
cons: Drift visibility: adjustment may occur without human review

decisions.rationale: Drift visibility decides the choice: human review provides a controlled response when quality changes. This gives up the faster response automated adjustment may offer.
consequences: Operators need a review and redeployment process.
Drift alerts require timely human attention.
